controls: Separate two-test corpus compares complete cached/cold offer fragments, ten changed compatibility/Type/law facts, exact request contents despite equal identities, malformed requests, precision eligibility, four-entry FIFO and final borrowed-owner release. Ordinary six-case Std corpus compares exact Plans, kernel reports, outputs and refusals.

boundary.phase_comparison: One actual math/near Source through StdHost::prepare_numerical_realizations: first cold call plus 32 repeated calls. Source parsing/checking/expansion and initial Host creation are outside the phase counts. Every repeated advertisement equals the first, including generation.
boundary.fragment_control: 32 direct cold strategy-fragment constructions; all complete offer values equal the cold oracle. This seam accounts for most repeated preparation allocation.
boundary.candidate_owner: Separate candidate observation begins before StdHost::from_advertisement(seed.clone()), performs 33 ordinary preparations with exact-advertisement comparison, and ends after dropping the Host and cache. Source/catalogue inputs and seed advertisement prepared outside. No matched full-owner reference was measured.
boundary.allocator: Existing thread-local successful alloc/alloc_zeroed/realloc request counter. Does not measure bytes, RSS or peak memory.
boundary.lifetime: Four FIFO fragments per owning Host. Only immutable exact Gear keys, compatibility facts and offer metadata retained; temporary strategy/scratch owners drop in the cold factory. Weak owner controls prove borrowed fragments survive eviction and release after final drop.

limitations: Unoptimized pinned Rust 1.98.1 local test worker; uncalibrated timings, including concurrent compilation during some observations. No product latency or speedup claim.
Initial cold adds 110 allocation requests for keys and immutable ownership.
Retained source/Type structures are caller-admitted finite inputs. Four entries is not a byte-accurate memory reservation.
Only installed Near strategy metadata is reused; admission, reservations, Host publication, planning, scratch and mutable runtime state are rebuilt/revalidated normally.

Installed Back/artifact code is immutable for this process; nothing persists across a different binary. Source identities, full exact Gear contents and protocol/Host/Boot/profile bind reuse. Cached metadata is authority-free and never reuses authority decisions.
